scenes.heading: Building a contract that protects you

sents.d: Building a contract that protects you
The clauses that prevent the most common client disputes.
A short, clear contract prevents more disputes than a long, confusing one.

At minimum, include: a deposit due before work begins, a payment schedule tied to milestones (not just 'on completion'), a defined number of revision rounds, and who owns the raw footage versus the final edit.

scenes.heading: Add a kill fee and usage rights

sents.d: Add a cancellation or 'kill fee' clause covering work already done if a client cancels midway, and a usage rights section specifying where the client can use the final video (e.g. social media only vs. broadcast).
Having clients sign before any filming — not after — is the single biggest predictor of getting paid on time.

take: Get a short, clear contract signed before you film anything.
